chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Two greedy persons never get satiated: the seeker of knowledge, and the seeker of this world.
ai.seo_question: What are the two insatiable seekers mentioned in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) contrasts the insatiable nature of worldly desire with the boundless depth of true knowledge, a distinction central to Shia epistemology where 'ilm' is seen as a divine light rather than a finite commodity. This teaching underscores that while material pursuits are limited by their objects, the seeker of knowledge finds that each discovery reveals further mysteries, preventing spiritual satiety. This concept aligns with the Shia emphasis on continuous intellectual and spiritual growth (ijtihad and tadabbur) as an endless journey toward the Divine.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 457. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Two greedy persons never get satiated, the seeker of knowledge and the seeker of this world.
